heading_path: Adding outside collaborators to a repository
structuredContent.text:
## Adding outside collaborators to a repository

You can give outside collaborators access to a repository in your repository settings. For more information, see [AUTOTITLE](/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/managing-repository-settings/managing-teams-and-people-with-access-to-your-repository#inviting-a-team-or-person).

content.text:
**Design recommendation** (based on GitHub docs in this repo):

GitHub permissions are granted at the **repository** level, not per-issue — there's no built-in way to let a collaborator see only *some* issues within a shared repo (`content/repositories/.../disabling-issues.md`). So structure it as:

- **Organization** = your company account.
- **One repository per project** (or even per task, for freelancers) under the org.
- Add each freelancer as an **outside collaborator** on only the specific repo(s) containing their task — they get no visibility into other repos/customers (`content/organizations/managing-user-access-to-your-organizations-repositories/managing-outside-collaborators/adding-outside-collaborators-to-repositories-in-your-organization.md`, "Adding outside collaborators to a repository").
- Use **Teams** to group collaborators by customer/project instead of managing access one-by-one (`content/organizations/managing-peoples-access-to-your-organization-with-roles/roles-in-an-organization.md`, "Outside collaborators" section).
- Optionally restrict who *else* in your org can invite outside collaborators via org settings (`content/organizations/managing-organization-settings/setting-permissions-for-adding-outside-collaborators.md`).

Bottom line: since tasks can't be individually scoped, isolate each freelancer's task into its own repo.
